messages.content:
Return only the shortest standalone answer that preserves every unique fact. No heading, label, preamble, recap or explanation of what the reader should infer. Combine related facts into complete sentences; mention each fact once. Attach evidence IDs in parentheses. Prefer specific verbs and short clauses. Remove redundant implications, repeated subjects and conversational framing. Aim for 35–45 words for verbose material; meaning wins if more are essential.

Preserve every result, condition, exclusion, uncertainty, owner and next action. Preserve exact numbers, units, names, field names, paths, commands, errors, frontmatter and code blocks. Do not claim an instruction happened or an untested result passed. Check all source facts silently before answering.

Already concise: copy EXACTLY. Requested JSON: exact keys/types, no surrounding text. Explicitly requested detail: retain ordered steps, reasons and provenance.

Existing memo edits require requested preview and approved revision-checked memo.write. Stop on conflicts; preserve source evidence. Use one normal drafting call.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: reply.
Reply to a user asking why their saved edit was rejected.

Source:
The save was rejected because the document changed after the version that the user read. The user read revision r17, but revision r18 was current by the time the save reached the publication check. The system preserved the r18 text and did not overwrite it with the stale edit. The rejected edit has not been applied. This was a revision conflict, not a permission denial. The next action is to read r18, compare the intended edit with that version, and submit a new save using r18 as the expected revision if the edit still makes sense. There is no automatic retry. The diagnostic reference is save-check-9. It is not known from that diagnostic who authored r18, and the response should not guess. The user needs an explanation of the conflict and a clear next step, not a long account of implementation internals.

message.content: Your edit was rejected because the document changed after the version you read: you read revision r17, but r18 was current when your save reached the publication check. The system preserved r18 and did not overwrite it with your stale edit, so your edit was not applied. This was a revision conflict, not a permission denial. There is no automatic retry. Next, read r18, compare your intended edit against it, and submit a new save using r18 as the expected revision if the edit still makes sense. Diagnostic reference: save-check-9. The author of r18 is not known from that diagnostic.
